title: Young people spend a third of their leisure time on devices
meta_description: Is technology making us less sociable?  A look at how technology has influenced our leisure time

breadcrumb.text: Young people spend a third of their leisure time on devices

lede: Is technology making us less sociable? A look at how technology has influenced our leisure time.

body.text: 19 December 2017
Young people spent more than a third of their overall leisure time – around 14 hours per week – using a device in 2015, new analysis shows.
Men aged 25 and under use devices such as mobile phones, tablets, e-readers and laptops the most. Device use occupied 35% of their leisure time, whereas for women it was 29%.

body.h4: Percentage of leisure time spent using a device, by age and gender
body.text: The highest share of time devoted to device use was when people were pursuing hobbies, computing, or playing games which is to be expected, as computing naturally requires device use. Resting had the second highest share of device use, which can include searching the web and chatting using a mobile phone.

body.h4: Percentage of leisure time spent using a device, by age and gender
body.text: People in this age group are more likely to be heavier users of social media. This may explain their high use of devices compared with other age groups.

body.h3: People are spending less leisure time being active
body.text: People are spending less leisure time being active

body.h3: People are spending less leisure time being active
body.text: Compared to 2000, people in 2015 spent less of their leisure time, on average, on activities like sports and cultural pursuits. The 2015 survey included the category ‘device use’ which could contribute to the difference in other leisure pursuits.

body.h3: People are spending less leisure time being active
body.text: [Adults aged 19 to 64 are advised by the NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/Livewell/fitness/Pages/physical-activity-guidelines-for-adults.aspx) to undertake a mixture of aerobic and strength exercises every week. This could include 150 minutes of aerobic activity and two days per week spent doing exercises that use all muscle groups.

body.h3: People are spending less leisure time being active
body.text: [In 2015 to 2016, 26% of adults in England were classified as inactive](https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/613532/obes-phys-acti-diet-eng-2017-rep.pdf) (carrying out less than 30 minutes of physical activity per week). [According to the NHS](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/health-matters-getting-every-adult-active-every-day/health-matters-getting-every-adult-active-every-day), people in the UK are around 20% less active now than they were in the 1960s.

body.h3: People are spending less leisure time being active
body.text: The NHS says this is down to varying factors like the rise of car ownership, and more recently, the popularity of sedentary activities such as playing video games and computing.

body.h3: Are we becoming less sociable?
body.text: Are we becoming less sociable?

body.h3: Are we becoming less sociable?
body.text: In 2015, people spent an average of around six hours per week socialising – a fall of 12.7% since 2000. When compared with total leisure time available – 38 hours per week for women and 43 hours per week for men – this is a small amount of the total.

body.h3: Are we becoming less sociable?
body.text: Comparatively, mass media consumption, for example, reading, listening to music or watching television, accounts for around half of all leisure time taken. People may be using mobile phones to socialise when they’re watching television, but it’s not necessarily face-to-face communication.

body.h3: Are we becoming less sociable?
body.text: It’s possible that with increased device use, people are becoming less likely to go out of their way to meet up and socialise. Easy internet access enables people to talk to friends via social media apps, but they’re still doing so alone.

body.h3: Are we becoming less sociable?
body.text: The data show that, of all leisure time spent using a device, 46% of this time is spent alone compared with 29% without a device.
